public_rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. It says that if 'enough' other companies report poor returns on AI spending, the AI bubble pops. The source does not say how many companies would be enough. The packet has no count of such company reports, so it cannot show whether the condition has been met. Al Jazeera reported that after the October 22, 2026 sell-off, the Nasdaq Composite was about 5.8 percent below its all-time high of October 6 (e1). The same report says Meta raised its projected capital spending for the year to $135bn to $145bn (e2). This is one company's plan and says nothing about AI investment as a whole. A 5.8 percent drop in the Composite does not meet the early-resolution rule, which needs a fall of 20 percent or more in leading AI stocks or the Nasdaq-100 plus broad AI capex cuts. The condition is undefined and there is no deadline, so market levels so far do not contradict the forecast either.
limitations: The packet has no evidence on how many companies have publicly reported poor AI returns.
'Enough' and 'pops' are not defined in the source.
The market evidence comes from one news report, covers only the period up to October 23, 2026, and refers to the Nasdaq Composite, not the Nasdaq-100 or a basket of leading AI stocks.
The capital spending evidence covers only Meta's projection. It does not show the direction of AI investment across the industry.

our_interpretation: Antecedent: many companies beyond Uber publicly report that AI spending is not producing proportional productivity gains. 'Enough' is not defined.

Consequent: the AI investment bubble 'pops', read plainly as a sharp, lasting collapse in AI-linked valuations and investment (for example a bear market of 20% or more in leading AI stocks, together with clear cuts to AI spending).
criteria.support_condition: Many companies are documented publicly reporting poor AI returns, followed by a sharp, lasting collapse in AI valuations or investment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Many companies clearly report poor AI returns, yet AI valuations and investment stay high or keep rising for a long time.
